You are a repo feature worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repository, detached at HEAD. Edit files here directly.

OWNERSHIP: you own exactly three paths, factory/outbox_push.py, factory/outbox_listen.py, and tests/test_packet_id_flow.py (new). Do NOT modify, create, delete, or reformat anything else. Do NOT git commit or push, do NOT run git add -A. Leave changes uncommitted; the check exports them.

CONTEXT, A REAL FAILURE HAPPENING RIGHT NOW. An AI agent on a second machine raised an approval packet carrying a packet_id it generated. That packet became a Linear card, the owner tapped Approve on his phone, and the decision was recorded here. The agent still cannot see the answer, because it polls on packet_id and the decision row only carries card_identifier. It is waiting correctly, forever, on a system that is failing it. Your job is to make the packet_id survive the whole journey.

READ FIRST, READ-ONLY: factory/outbox_push.py (_append_ledger and its call site; note how packet_text and urgency already travel from the packet onto the ledger row), factory/outbox_listen.py (the decision row built in tick, and _resume_context), and tests/test_outbox_push.py plus tests/test_outbox_listen.py for style.

CHANGE 1, in factory/outbox_push.py. When the outbox packet carries a packet_id, put it on the ledger row. This is the same path packet_text and urgency already take. A packet WITHOUT a packet_id must still push cleanly; not every caller uses one.

CHANGE 2, in factory/outbox_listen.py. When the ledger row for a card carries a packet_id, the DECISION row must carry it too, for every decision type: approve, skip and fix. On a fix it must appear alongside the existing resume context, because the remote agent needs both the id and the notes to revise. Omit the field cleanly when the ledger row has none.

DO NOT CHANGE: card-level grouping by card_identifier, the human-owned FIX behaviour (card parks in Agent Needs Input, stays open, owner recorded), the agent-marker skip list, the buzz sender, the stall sensor, the urgency handling, the cursor and row-hash dedup, or any fail-closed path.

WRITE tests/test_packet_id_flow.py proving the ROUND TRIP: push a packet carrying a packet_id through outbox_push with a fake card sender, then run outbox_listen against the ledger push just produced with a fake reader returning an APPROVE comment, and assert the decision row carries that same packet_id. That end-to-end assertion is the one that would have caught this; a test of either half alone would not. Also cover a packet with no packet_id pushing cleanly.

VERIFY from the worktree root: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider. The whole suite must stay green.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave the three owned files edited and uncommitted, and write ./notes.md at the ROOT of your worktree recording what you read, what you changed, the verification command and its result, and any assumption.

HARD RULES: no new dependencies, no network, no allow-on-failure paths. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Do not capture anything to any memory or brain service.

tasks.spec:
You are a repo feature worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the loop-factory repository, detached at HEAD. Edit files here directly.

OWNERSHIP: you own exactly two paths, factory/decision_push_back.py (new) and tests/test_decision_push_back.py (new). Do NOT modify, create, delete, or reformat anything else. Do NOT git commit or push, do NOT run git add -A. Leave changes uncommitted; the check exports them.

CONTEXT. Agents run on more than one machine. A second machine raises approval packets into its local outbox; this box pulls them, cards them, buzzes the owner's phone, and records his decision. What is missing is the return leg: nothing carries the recorded decision back to the machine that asked. Right now an agent on that machine is waiting on an approval the owner has already given. You are building the leg that closes that circle.

READ FIRST, READ-ONLY: factory/remote_outbox_pull.py, which is the mirror image of what you are building and establishes the conventions for append-only merge, atomic write, local-vs-ssh transport and fail-closed behaviour; and factory/outbox_listen.py to see the shape of a decision row.

BUILD factory/decision_push_back.py with this CLI:
  python3 factory/decision_push_back.py --decisions <path> --department <name> --dest <path> [--ssh-host <user@host>] [--identity <keyfile>]
Behaviour:
1. Read the local decisions file. Select ONLY rows whose department matches --department AND which carry a non-empty packet_id. A row for another department must never be written to this machine: that is a cross-surface leak. A row without a packet_id is useless to the remote agent, which polls on packet_id, so skip it and say how many were skipped.
2. APPEND-ONLY MERGE into --dest, matching factory/remote_outbox_pull.py's approach. Running twice must add nothing; the remote agent must not see the same answer twice. A newly recorded decision must arrive on the next run.
3. Carry the WHOLE decision row across, including notes on a fix decision. Without the notes the remote agent knows it was asked to change something but not what.
4. When --ssh-host is absent, --dest is a plain LOCAL path. This is how the tool is verified without a second machine and the check uses it. When present, write over ssh using --identity if supplied. Never read, print or log the identity file's contents.
5. FAIL CLOSED AND NON-DESTRUCTIVE. A missing or unreadable decisions file, or an unreachable destination, must exit nonzero with a printed reason and leave --dest exactly as it was. Never truncate what the remote already has.
6. An empty selection is a QUIET SUCCESS: exit 0 and report 0 rows. Nothing to send is the normal state most of the time, and a leg that goes red every tick trains the operator to ignore it.
7. Print a one-line summary of rows added and rows skipped, so a timer log is readable.

WRITE tests/test_decision_push_back.py covering: only the named department crosses; rows without packet_id are skipped and counted; idempotency; a new decision arriving; fix notes surviving; empty selection exiting 0; and a missing decisions file exiting nonzero without truncating the destination.

VERIFY from the worktree root: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider. The whole suite must stay green.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave the two owned files edited and uncommitted, and write ./notes.md at the ROOT of your worktree recording what you read, what you changed, the verification command and its result, and any assumption.

HARD RULES: no new dependencies, no allow-on-failure paths, no credential read or logged. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Do not capture anything to any memory or brain service.
